full_judgment: 2. The respondents instituted Title Suit No. 57 of 1999 in the 1st Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Narayanganj for declaration of title and recovery of khas pogsession contending, inter alia, that "Ka" schedule property appertaining to C.S. Plot No. 78 comprising an area of 151 decimals of land fell in the saham of Kalai and Ahmed, and other co-sharers got other lands. Thereafter by an amicable partition between them Kalai got a share of 90 decimals of land and Ahmed got the rest 69 decimals out of 1.50 acres of land. During C.S. operation Kalai and Ahmed being found in possession their names were duly recorded to the extent of 1.59 acres of land. As they failed to pay rents, the landlord Ashutosh Banerjee got a decree for arrears of rent in Rent Suit No. 2526 of 1929 in the 4th Court of Munsif, Narayaranganj, and in pursuance of Rent Execution Case No. 45 of 1933 the landlord purchased 90 decimals of land. The sale certificate was registered through Court in favour of Ashutosh Benerjee on 17th July, 1933, and thereafter the landlord auction purchaser settled 80 decimals of land from the east- cm side in favour of one Kamar Ali and while he was owning and possessing the same, he transfeged 40 decimals of land to Rekmat Ali by registered deed No. 2513 dated 25th February, 1948 and thereafter Kamar Ali also transferred 40 decimals of land to Rekmat Ali and accordingly Rekmat Ali became owner in possession of entire 80 decimals of land. Ramat Ali died leaving behind his wife Golbahar Bibi, four sons namely, Monsur Ali, Montazuddin, Sukkur Ali and. Jainuddin and one daughter Asi Khatun. The Munsur Ali got 40 decimals of land from southern side and Momtazuddin got 40 decimals out of 80 decimals from their father Rekmat Ali by amicable family arrangement. Momtazuddin transferred his entire 40 decimals of land to his daughter Batashi by registered deed dated 11th October, 1966(Ext. 5). The R.S. Khatian No. 1630 has been prepared in her name for this 40 decimals of land and R.S. Khatian No. 1854 (l3xt.9) has been prepared in the name of MunSur Ali in respect of 37 decimals but in fact he had 40 decimals of land out of which 30 decimals had been acquired by the government in L. A. Case No. 140 of 1962-60 and while owning and possessing the remaining 10 decimals of land, Munsur All died leaving the plaintiffs as his heirs  and then they were dispossessed by the defendants on 7th April, 1999.
